errors.problem: Elative tap glosses are fixed to one sense regardless of the construction: أَقْدَمُ مِنْ ('older than') is tapped as 'the oldest (before a noun)' in the very quiz that teaches the comparative; أَكْبَرُ مَدِينَة ('the biggest city') is tapped as 'bigger'; أَكْثَرُ الْبَدْوِ ('most of the Bedouin') as 'more'; اِبْنُهُ الْأَكْبَر ('his eldest son') as 'the biggest'. The segs of the same sentences are right; only the taps are wrong.
errors.fix: tap glosses: أَقْدَمُ → 'older; the oldest', أَكْبَرُ → 'bigger; the biggest', أَكْثَرُ → 'more; most (of)', الْأَكْبَر → 'the biggest, the eldest'

notes.note: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا أُسْتَاذ سَامِي: as a vocative in iḍāfa the title would take -a (يَا أُسْتَاذَ سَامِي); the course leaves the vowel off mid-sentence. Owner's call whether to vocalise it.
سُوقٌ قَدِيمٌ treats سُوق as masculine; in MSA the word is more often feminine (سُوقٌ قَدِيمَةٌ), though both genders are attested. The chapter title أَسْوَاق قَدِيمَة is fine either way.

الْخُوَارِزْمِيُّ is vocalised khuwārizmī (consistent throughout) while the English prose writes al-Khwārizmī; Arabic sources also vocalise الخَوارزمي (khawārizmī). Name spelling, consistent, so not counted.
اسْمُ is written without the kasra on the hamzat waṣl here but اِسْمُ everywhere else; no effect on sound or transliteration.
'the month of الْحَجّ': the month is ذُو الْحِجَّة (Dhū l-Ḥijja); 'the month of the Hajj' is a paraphrase, not the month's name. Clearer: 'the tenth day of Dhū l-Ḥijja, the month of the pilgrimage'.
'decorated for رَمَضَان, 2004' — the year reads oddly in a caption; check the photo date is wanted.
Caption identifies the pyramids by position (Menkaure's nearest, then Khafre's and Khufu's); only true for a photo taken from the south-west. Check against the actual image.
مَرِيئًا is glossed 'and may it be wholesome'; the 'and' is not in the word (the phrase هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا has no conjunction). Harmless.
Transliteration 'l-ḥayāh' for الْحَيَاة follows ALA-LC (ā + tāʾ marbūṭa → āh); fine, just unlike the '-a' the learner sees elsewhere.
أَشْرَبُ فِنْجَانَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثَة is elliptical (full form ثَلَاثَةَ فَنَاجِين); natural in speech, acceptable.
Culture: Libya also uses the Western digits alongside Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia; the sentence is not wrong, just incomplete.
Culture: Wadi Rum was listed by UNESCO in 2011 as a mixed natural/cultural site; the text's claim is correct but a year could be added like the other sites.
The transliteration line converts the Arabic-Indic digits ٠ ١ ٢ ٣ into 0 1 2 3, so the example '٢٨ is 28' reads '28 is 28' in the ⟶ view. Engine display quirk, no learning effect.
All quiz and reading-question answer keys in the nine chapters were checked and are correct; all mistakes[].wrong/right pairs and their 'why' explanations are correct.

summary: Checked all nine Explore chapters (calligraphy, coffee, desert, family, food, places, ramadan, science, souq): every Arabic title, body-text word, sentence, mistake pair, word entry, reading and quiz, with their harakat, case endings (diptotes إِيرَانَ / إِسْحَاقَ / مَلَابِسَ / دِمَشْقَ, accusative after كَانَ and لٰكِنَّ, number–noun gender in بِعَشَرَةِ رِيَالَاتٍ), agreement, verb forms, translations, literals, segs, tap glosses, answer keys and the generated transliteration. The Arabic itself is clean: I found no major error and no sentence a learner would copy wrongly. The 12 findings are all minor: 7 tap-gloss mismatches where a word shows the sense written for another sentence (كَرِيم as 'Karim (first name)' in رَمَضَان كَرِيم, يَد 'hand luggage', وَادِي 'Wadi Musa', elatives أَقْدَمُ/أَكْبَرُ/أَكْثَرُ fixed to one of their two senses, يَصُومُ, تَفَضَّلْ, بَارِدًا '(object)'), one vocalisation inconsistency (الْمَصْرِيّ vs the quiz's al-Miṣrī), and 4 engine transliteration quirks reported once each (shāī, final -w as ū, no waṣla elision after tanwīn, capitalisation of names after وَ and al-). All quiz and reading answer keys are correct. 14 notes for the owner cover a vocative vowel, the gender of سُوق, the Khwārizmī vowel, a few culture/caption details and harmless display quirks.
